item.title: Clemson players highlight ‘Support Swinney’ sign after beating Duke
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Zachary Taft-Imagn Images Clemson players highlight ‘Support Swinney’ sign after beating Duke appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Clemson Tigers heard the outside noise all week, and they answered it with a statement win for head coach Dabo Swinney on his 57th birthday. Following Friday night’s 20-10 road upset over the Duke Blue Devils in Durham, N.C., Clemson players rallied on the sideline to hold up a fan-made “Support Swinney” poster while chanting “Dabo” and singing “Happy Birthday.” Offensive linemen Harris Sewell and Grant Wise led the postgame tribute after a turbulent week in which critics questioned Swinney’s program following a loss to the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets and his bold national title guarantee. Instead of folding as double-digit underdogs, the Tigers dominated the trenches to improve to 7-4 overall and 5-3 in ACC play. ‘Support Swinney’ sign and ‘Dabo’ chant making their way into Clemson’s postgame celebrations @ClemsonFB beats Duke 20-10 pic.twitter.com/GTLbQtlfOb Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Caroline Soro (@caroline_soro) November 21, 2026 Clemson controlled the clock for 37:15 and piled up 384 total yards behind a ground-and-pound attack that churned out 220 rushing yards. Making his first career start, third-string quarterback Trent Pearman efficiently managed the offense, completing 17 of 27 passes for 164 yards without a turnover while adding 51 rushing yards and a 9-yard touchdown run on six carries. Wide receiver-turned-quarterback Chris Denson also punished Duke’s front with 71 yards and a 7-yard fourth-quarter score on 16 rushes, while running back Jarvis Green paced the backfield with 84 yards on 16 carries. Wideout T.J. Moore hauled in four catches for 68 yards, and kicker Nolan Hauser drilled field goals from 36 and 39 yards. On the other side of the ball, Clemson’s defense smothered Duke, limiting the Blue Devils to 247 yards and 11 first downs. Linebacker Fletcher Cothran recorded a sack, and safety Corey Myrick sealed the momentum with an interception against Duke quarterback Walker Eget, who went 16 of 38 for 149 yards. Aside from running back Nate Sheppard’s 116 rushing yards and 55-yard touchdown burst, Duke found zero room to breathe. Critics may still doubt Clemson’s ceiling, but inside that locker room, the Tigers clearly have Swinney’s back. item.title: Oregon kicker Gage Hurych scores on trick-play run
item.description: EAST LANSING, Mich. – If style and flash are what the College Football Playoff ranking committee wants to see from teams contending for the postseason, Oregon obliged Oct. 20 at Michigan State. The No. 13 Ducks put together a performance that included another highlight-reel touchdown catch from star receiver Dakorien Moore, a breakout performance from third-string running back Brandon Smith, a stingy, two-takeaway effort by the defense, and oh yeah, a touchdown run by their kicker on a fake field-goal attempt. Gage Hurych, the former standout lacrosse player from West Linn High School, scored on a 15-yard run at the end of the first half to ignite Oregon’s 45-7 win against Michigan State Friday night at Spartan Stadium. It was the fourth straight win for the Ducks (8-3, 6-2 Big Ten Conference), who continue their late-season push to make the CFP. “We knew that we had to be able to take advantage of opportunities to be able to go out there and score,” Oregon’s Dan Lanning said. “I think once we kind of figured that out it allowed us to go out there and show what I think we are, which is one of the best teams here down the stretch.” Hurych’s score – a play three seasons in the making – electrified the Oregon sideline and ignited the Ducks after an otherwise sluggish first half. With seven seconds to go before halftime, the Ducks lined up for a 35-yard field-goal attempt. But instead, holder Bailey Ettridge took the snap and flipped it to Hurych, who ran to his left, shook off one attempted tackle and dove into the end zone. The Oregon sidelined erupted in celebration after the play. “Coach Lanning about punched the air out of me when (Hurych) he scored,” quarterback Dylan Raiola said. “It definitely did get the guys going,” beamed Hurych, a junior in his first season as the Ducks’ primary kicker. “I mean, guys have seen that in practice for literally three years. I think everybody’s been waiting for that call to go for it.” The play was reviewed, as it appeared Hurych’s right leg might have hit the ground at the 1-yard line before he crossed into the end zone. But the call on the field stood and Oregon took a 17-0 lead into halftime. “My knee didn’t touch the ground, for the record,” said Hurych, who became the first Oregon kicker to rush for a touchdown since Paul Martinez on Sept. 9, 2006 versus Fresno State. “I’m glad it was at the 15-yard line and not the 16,” Lanning joked. “Gage just said if we ever call it, I’m going to score and he did that today.” Hurych’s touchdown was the highlight, but the entire scoring drive was impressive, considering that when it began with 1:41 to play in the half, the Ducks had only 92 yards of offense. item.description: ‘Too many avoidable goals’: Maresca warns Manchester City to tighten up at the back Enzo Maresca has said Manchester City must stop conceding 'avoidable goals' as the club look to end their winless run. Manchester City headed into the international break on a run of three consecutive Premier League defeats. The Cityzens lost to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest in succession, to fall six points adrift of Arsenal in the title race. Defensive lapses have been evident, while goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma has faced scrutiny for his performances. Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Fulham this afternoon, Maresca warned his side that they must tighten up defensively. "I was not thinking we were doing everything well when we were winning games. I’m not thinking we did everything wrong when we lost games," he said. "There are things we need to do better and no doubt we will do better. "We are conceding too many goals. Most of them are avoidable. So we need to avoid mistakes and try to deal with it [better] when it happens." item.title: Luka Doncic, Walker Kessler React To JJ Redick’s Fiery Locker Room Outburst In Lakers’ Comeback Win vs. Kings
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA - NOVEMBER 20: Walker Kessler #14, Luka Doncic #77, and Head Coach JJ Redick of the Los Angeles Lakers talk during the game against the Sacramento Kings during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 20, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images) The Lakers fought back from an 11-point third-quarter deficit to steal a 106-104 win over the Kings tonight, despite not playing their best on both ends of the floor early. After the game, JJ Redick was asked how he managed to rally the troops and motivate the Lakers at halftime, when they headed to the locker room down by eight points. “I feel like I did a decent job of regulating [team emotions] at halftime; they may have a different opinion of that. I can’t repeat every word I used, but the main message was we got to be tougher; we got to bring a little bit of energy,” JJ Redick said at his postgame press conference. Luka Doncic and Walker Kessler recalled the incident differently, but the team took the message maturely instead of getting in their feelings about what JJ Redick said. “Yeah, I mean, he yells. I’m used to it,” Luka Doncic said as the room broke out into laughter. “But it got us all fired up. So sometimes it’s good to hear.” Luka Doncic had a rough night from behind the three-point line, especially. He finished with 25 points, eight assists, four rebounds, and two steals, shooting 9-18 from the field (50.0% FG) and 2-9 from beyond the arc (22.2% 3P). Doncic sat out most of the fourth quarter and took only one field-goal attempt in the five minutes he played. The Lakers needed their other players to step up as the defense kept swarming the Slovenian superstar. In a game where Zach LaVine missed a good look for a game-winner at the final buzzer, Walker Kessler missed two crucial free throws that could have put the game out of the Kings’ reach before the final possession. Walker Kessler also had a relatively slow night, scoring just six of his 15 points in the first half. He finished with 15 points, seven rebounds, two assists, three blocks, and one steal while shooting 7-11 from the field (63.6% FG). Kessler suggested that some of Redick’s halftime outburst in the locker room was directed at him. “He lit me up a little bit. Rightfully so,” said Kessler on JJ Redick’s message to the team at halftime. “It was constructive. He was like, ‘I know you can do this. Do it,’” Kessler explained . Sometimes, nights like this remind you of the fierce competition and excess of talent in the league, and how even a bottom team like the Kings is testing the nerves of a playoff contender like the Lakers. Fortunately, the Lakers somehow held on to the lead they gained down the stretch and came away with the win. Otherwise, JJ Redick may have had another outburst at the team after the final buzzer. item.title: Antonelli fastest but penalty leaves Verstappen on pole
item.description: Kimi Antonelli won both the previous two grands prix in the United States this season, in Miami and Austin [Getty Images] Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix but a grid penalty will hand pole position to Red Bull's Max Verstappen. Antonelli, running at the back of the pack of cars in qualifying and maximising his tow, beat Verstappen by 0.258 seconds. But the new world champion has a five-place grid penalty for using more than permitted number of engine components and will start sixth. The Italian's team-mate George Russell was just 0.073secs behind Verstappen and will start alongside the Dutchman on the front row. McLaren's Lando Norris qualified fourth, and will start third, ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar. Both Ferraris were eliminated in the second session and qualified 11th and 12th with Charles Leclerc ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Each will be promoted a place by a 10-place penalty for McLaren's Oscar Piastri, who qualified seventh. Racing Bulls' rookie Arvid Lindblad, sixth fastest, is the last driver to be promoted as a result of Antonelli's penalty. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson will start seventh with Alpine's Pierre Gasly eighth and Franco Colapinto ninth. Drivers limited to 27 laps for tyres in Qatar Antonelli's final run did not start auspiciously as he and Russell became tangled up with the Alpines and Racing Bulls as they sought the best track position to optimise the slipstream effect. Antonelli ended up the last driver to run and made it to the line with only one second to spare before the chequered flag, one second behind Lindblad. Normally, being so close to the car in front would be a compromise but in Las Vegas it magnified the tow effect and Antonelli leapt to the front. "That was all the tow," he said over the radio after being told he was on pole. "Starting the lap, I was only one second behind the car in front and I thought I was screwed," he said. "But the tow is so powerful here." Verstappen, who has won two of the three Las Vegas Grands Prix, said: "I have been struggling with some weird issues that were also in the car in Brazil and just trying to get my head around how to deal with that. "In qualifying we managed to make it work. Had a solid qualifying. My first lap in qualifying was pretty much as good as it could be with the tow, so to be on the front row is good for us. "It was solid in the corners, and you have a bit of dirty air, but it is insane how much you gain on the straights." Russell had looked in the running for the pole, but was happy with his session despite missing out. "Overall it's been a very solid session and a solid day," he said. "I wanted to be on pole but I am probably more pleased with the performance than in Mexico when I was on the front row. "Kimi did a great job and he probably thought it wasn't going to work out so well being so close but with the tow it worked out." item.description: Florian Wirtz primed for overdue Anfield moment as Liverpool host Pochettino's Man United originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Manchester United know all about a giant of the past looming, for better or worse, over the present. Mauricio Pochettino will start his tenure in the unforgiving surroundings of Anfield, United's ninth manager since Sir Alex Ferguson's departure in 2013. Ferguson famously pledged to knock Liverpool off their perch and made good on those desires. The modern-day United are scrambling around on the bottom of the cage, flapping about in the muck of 18th position in the Premier League. That is an unfathomably low ebb for the dominant club of the Premier League era, but every manager since Ferguson has measured up poorly. Pochettino will begin the work of snapping that long sequence as Merseyside bays for Mancunian blood on Sunday. That passage of time is perhaps on the Argentine's side. Flipping the focus to Liverpool, Arne Slot followed in Jurgen Klopp's footsteps and instantly won the Premier League, only to be out of a job a year later after a poor title defence. Slot salvaged Champions League qualification, but the direction of travel wasn't encouraging. It also didn't feel great. Under Klopp, the vibes were immaculate. "He’s that kind of special talent. “Liverpool don’t need any tips from us; he’s already in much better form there now. It’s just a different style of play. item.title: Ao Tanaka's four-word Brazil reunion and the missing piece he's started to find
item.description: Ao Tanaka's four-word Brazil reunion and the missing piece he's started to find Ao Tanaka is a man of few words but a man of many skills, says his boss. The 28-year-old's taciturn nature was portrayed perfectly by a recent interaction with a former colleague on international duty. Japan's fixture with Brazil handed Tanaka a reunion with Lucas Perri, who is out on loan this season with Torino in Serie A. Farke was keen to find out how the pair got on, so asked his midfielder. "Everyone seems to speak about Ao Tanaka," said Farke. "The only one who never seems to speak is Ao Tanaka himself. So we had a short conversation about how it was for him to see Lucas Perri in the game against Brazil. Ao said, 'I said hello...and goodbye. That's it.' So this is how Ao Tanaka is. So he is not a man of many words, but of many skills on the football pitch. And we all love him." His form of late has attracted praise. And numbers back it up. No midfielder in the Premier League presses passing lanes more than Tanaka, who is Leeds' best tackler on Gradient Sports data. What Farke has seen in his midfielder is a level of consistency that was difficult to acquire as he found his feet in the Premier League. "It was a big ask for him after spending many years on second-tier level in Germany or here in the Championship," said Farke. "Last season was his first year in the top league, Premier League level. I think he had also shown glimpses of his potential, but he needed to find a bit of this consistency. And I would also agree that he is finding this during the season. "So it was not always a 10 out of 10 performance, but I think it's important for a player once you're mature that on the weaker days you're still a six or a seven out of 10. And this is what he's doing. So on perhaps even the more challenging days, he's at least solid and plays first of all with good confidence, like he always does, but also with a seriousness to be consistent and to work for the team and also against the ball." Tanaka's tackling prowess is also borne out by data. Gradient say only two players in the Premier League win more tackles per 90 minutes than the Japan international. That's an area in which he has pleased his boss, who still wants more. "Strong in the duels, still sometimes decision-making and in front of the goal he can be a bit calmer," said Farke. "But overall, I think he's on a really good path to mature more and more. And if you do this, then you become more and more important for us. And we're all happy that he is in such a shape at the moment."

item.title: Rising star to play at World Darts Championship
item.description: Henry Coates will make his debut at the PDC World Darts Championships in December [PDC] A rising darts star is set to make his dreams a reality by playing at this year's World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace. Henry Coates, 20, secured his place in December's tournament after a breakthrough year which saw him become only the fifth player to win a Professional Darts Corporation (PDC) ranking title without a tour card . Coates, from Matlock, Derbyshire, also narrowly lost 5-4 to former world champion Michael van Gerwen during his "incredible" Grand Slam of Darts debut on Saturday. He qualified for the worlds by being a top player on the Challenge Tour Order of Merit rankings , determined by prize money won during the year. "The way that some of the results have gone in my favour means that I'm going to be playing at Ally Pally in December," said Coates. "I'm going to achieve my dream of playing there." Coates narrowly lost 5-4 to former world champion Michael van Gerwen [PDC] Coates, who began playing darts when he was two, secured his qualification for the Grand Slam of Darts by winning his PDC ranking title in the summer. Being from a fifth generation family of butchers, with a shop in Darley Dale, Coates said it was "incredible" to make his debut in the televised competition. The debutant held his own against Van Gerwen but the three-time champion won the deciding leg to clinch a 5-4 win. Despite the close defeat, Coates ended his first Grand Slam on a high with a "better" 5-4 victory over Sweden's Jeffrey de Graaf. "I loved every minute of it. I played so well, even the crowd were chanting my name," he said. He said his phone had been buzzing "non-stop" with messages about his performance during his Grand Slam debut. Parents, Tanya and Nick said watching their son go from playing on a magnetic dartboard while still in nappies to competing against some of the best players in the world "still feels like a dream". His father admitted he still gets nervous watching his son play on the big stage. "I pace about and I have to turn it off because I want him to win and do well," he said. The PDC World Darts Championship, which takes place between 11 December and 3 January, sees a total of 128 players competing to become world champion and claim £1m prize money. This year's event will be held in the Alexandra Palace's Great Hall, for the first time, meaning new attendance records will be set. With his opponents for the tournament still yet to be revealed, Coates hopes a good performance event will take his career to even greater heights. item.title: Max Verstappen responds to George Russell after Vegas clash
item.description: Motorsport photo During the final practice session for the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, Max Verstappen and George Russell crossed paths once again. The Dutchman overtook the Mercedes driver, but then slowed down in front of him and, according to the stewards, changed direction several times. Russell subsequently went down the inside of the four-time world champion, leading to contact between the two at Turn 14. It earned both rivals a trip to the stewards, although they ultimately dealt with the incident by issuing a warning. Unlike a reprimand, a warning carries no consequences at all. When Verstappen was asked about the incident during the press conference after qualifying, the Dutchman had little interest in discussing it. Asked what had happened, he simply replied: "Nothing. Nothing happened." Russell, however, subsequently launched a scathing attack on the Red Bull driver in the media pen. Speaking to Sky Sports Italy, Russell said, among other things: "I’m not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they’re bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody has got to stand up to that guy." Verstappen was largely unmoved. When Motorsport.com asked him about the clash during the Dutch media session that followed in the Las Vegas paddock, he replied: "I don't even want to waste my time on that. It's not worth it to me at all." Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing When it was pointed out that the stewards had referred in the FIA document to a gentlemen's agreement during preparation laps, under which drivers are expected to maintain their positions and avoid interfering with one another before starting a flying lap, Verstappen responded: "I've never seen such an agreement in my life." The stewards also made clear that they had attached little weight to the gentlemen's agreement mentioned by Russell in reaching their decision, instead focusing on the actions of both drivers. "The Stewards noted these explanations but considered that such informal understandings were of limited relevance to the assessment of the incident. The decisive considerations were the actual movements of both cars and their relative positions." It is particularly notable that the two drivers will share the front row of the grid in Vegas on Saturday night following Kimi Antonelli's grid penalty, but Verstappen insists the clash has not given him any extra motivation to keep Russell behind. "No, that's definitely not where I get my motivation from." item.description: Washington's Brooke Carlson drives past Stanford's Shay Ijiwoye on Friday night in during the Huskies' 105-50 win in Seattle. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Brynn McGaughy scored 21 points, Avery Howell added 20 and No. 16 Washington hit 17 3-pointers en route to a 105-50 win over Stanford on Friday night in Seattle, the most lopsided loss in program history for the Cardinal. Stanford (4-2), which had won four in a row since a season-opening loss to Arizona, saw the Huskies (5-0) post a 12-0 run to take a 20-4 lead in the first quarter. The Cardinal trailed by 15 after the first quarter, by 30 at halftime and by 41 entering the fourth quarter. Hailee Swain, who had scored at least 20 points in each of Stanford's first five games, led the Cardinal with 12 points. Stanford's 55-point margin of defeat topped a 49-point loss to Notre Dame on Feb. 6, 2025. Washington also matched the most points ever scored against the Cardinal, first achieved by Tennessee in a 105-69 win on Dec. 1, 1994. Cal 70, Hawaii 49: Albina Syla scored 16 points, Zara Russell added 14 and Naya Ojukwu had 10 as the Bears (6-0) beat the Rainbow Wahine (1-4) in the North Shore Showcase in Laie, Hawaii. The Bears, playing without leading scorer Lulu Twidale and Mjracle Sheppard because of injuries, led by four at halftime but pushed the margin to 10 on a three-point play by Ojukwu with 1:27 left in the third quarter. Cal led by double figures the rest of the way. "We had a lot of people step up with Lulu being out," Cal coach Charmin Smith said. "I love how Albina stepped up. item.title: Lakers’ win over Kings fueled by JJ Redick’s halftime speech
item.description: Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) celebrates a made three from his assist during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Friday November 20th, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. LOS ANGELES — Walker Kessler picked up three fouls before halftime, and the Lakers went to the locker room down eight to a one-win Sacramento team. JJ Redick had a message for the group and a more pointed one for his starting center. “We got to be tougher, we got to bring a little bit of energy,” Redick said of his halftime message. “He definitely lit into me and it was good,” Kessler said. “I needed it. That’s what makes a good coach.” Kessler helped the Lakers erase an 11-point third-quarter deficit, and Quentin Grimes hit a step-back 3-pointer with 56.3 seconds remaining to lift Los Angeles to a 106-104 win over the Kings on Friday night at Crypto.com Arena. The Lakers improved to 14-3 overall and 2-1 in NBA Cup West Group C, picking up their 10th win in 11 games and ending a homestand that had them play three games in a four-day span. Luka Dončić, who led the Lakers with 25 points and eight assists, was asked whether Redick’s halftime talk was more than a talk, which is how Redick put it after the game. “Yeah, I mean, he yells. I’m used to it,” Dončić said. “But it got us all fired up. So sometimes it’s good to hear.” The response took a few possessions. Sacramento stretched its lead to 67-56 early in the third quarter, but Jarred Vanderbilt grabbed two offensive rebounds in the period and threw down a dunk that brought the Lakers within two heading into the fourth. Kessler gave L.A. the lead 18 seconds into the final quarter with his first 3-pointer as a Laker. He later broke an 89-89 tie with a cutting layup off a pass from Collin Sexton, who scored six points in the first five minutes of the quarter. Kessler finished with 15 points, seven rebounds and three blocks. Matisse Thybulle added 14 points on 4-for-5 shooting from beyond the arc and set up Grimes for the deciding shot. The Lakers led by eight with 4:50 left before the Kings tied it twice. De’Andre Hunter, who scored a game-high 30 points, made a driving bank shot to even the score at 103 before Grimes hit his only 3-pointer of the night. Zach LaVine made one of two free throws to bring Sacramento within two and Kessler missed both of his attempts with 5.3 seconds left which gave the Kings a last chance shot on the final possession from LaVine. LaVine’s potential game-winning 3-pointer hit from the rim at the buzzer that crushed any possibility of sending fans heartbroken. Grimes finished with 13 points and seven assists. Austin Reaves missed his fourth consecutive game with a left heel bruise, and the Lakers will host Utah again Monday at 7 p.m. PT.

item.title: 'We don't have references' - Andoni Iraola warns Liverpool of Man Utd's tactical 'advantage' under Mauricio Pochettino
item.description: Andoni Iraola Liverpool - getty Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola admits Manchester United hold a clear tactical advantage ahead of Sunday's massive Premier League showdown at Anfield. The Reds boss believes Mauricio Pochettino's sudden arrival in the Old Trafford dugout makes their historic rivals dangerously unpredictable. Iraola wary of unpredictable Manchester United Iraola believes United hold a slight tactical advantage over Liverpool ahead of their massive Premier League clash on Sunday . The highly anticipated Anfield showdown marks Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of the visitors. Pochettino replaced Michael Carrick as United head coach during the recent international break. His sudden arrival at Old Trafford brings an element of surprise to a historic fixture that always demands maximum focus. Liverpool currently sit fourth in the Premier League table after an impressive start to the campaign. Conversely, their rivals will travel to Merseyside languishing in 18th place following a disastrous eight-game winless run. Adapting to Pochettino's new tactical blueprint Preparing for a newly appointed manager presents a unique challenge for any opposition. Iraola admits his coaching staff lack recent reference points to predict exactly how Pochettino will set up his starting line-up. "We've faced each other [as managers] and obviously he has a lot of Premier League games behind him that we can look at," Iraola told reporters. "We can look at games from the U.S. but it's true that [United] have this small advantage that we don't have references to prepare because they can go different ways that we honestly don't know right now." Historic rivalry demands massive Anfield performance While the element of surprise favours the visitors, Iraola remains confident in his squad's ability to solve problems on the pitch. He stressed that the core strengths and weaknesses of the United players remain largely unchanged. However, the hosts must overcome a concerning psychological hurdle this weekend. Liverpool have surprisingly failed to beat the Red Devils at Anfield since March 2023, making this clash even more significant for the home support. "We have to adapt to certain things and I hope that we already have some time with the players and we can manage the beginning as quickly as possible," Iraola added. item.title: Cobblers women hoping for more games at Sixfields
item.description: Northampton Town Women play in FAWNL Division One Midlands [Getty Images] The manager of Northampton Town Women said he wanted the team to play more games at the home of the men's team. The FA Women's National League (FAWNL) Division One Midlands side take on table-topping Barnsley at Sixfields Stadium in Northampton on Sunday. While the team usually played at a non-league ground on the outskirts of Northampton, they also play at men's stadium, drawing crowds of more than 1,000. Matt Vernon, the team's manager, said: "We love playing our home games where we do, but if we could play more at Sixfields, it'd be great." Northampton Town Women are ninth in the table, but have won their last two league games. The two sides have met before at Sixfields, with the Cobblers winning 2-0 in October 2024. Women's team manager Matt Vernon said there was a very good infrastructure around the side [Getty Images] When speaking about Sixfields on BBC Radio Northampton's Cobblers Show , Vernon said: "Now that East Stand's finished, it's such a great stadium to play in. I can't imagine there's many better in League Two. "It really is the home of the football in the town, and it's a privilege to play there. "Some great players have played on that pitch, it's something that we mention to the players. "We don't try to overhype it, but for sure, they're all so keen to play games at Sixfields." At the end of September, Sports Alpha Capital, a Brazil-based consortium, took over Northampton Town and Vernon said: "The club is so behind the women and girls programme at the moment. "It's on a real upturn, you know, even from our younger junior teams and development pathways all the way up to the first team. "There's a real, real push and that can only be good." The men's team captain was among those encouraging fans to attend the games, which Vernon said the team appreciated. item.title: Lewis Hamilton reveals Ferrari F1 car damage after Las Vegas Q2 exit
item.description: Motorsport photo Lewis Hamilton put Ferrari's Q2 exit in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix down to energy deployment and floor damage, as the seven-time champion felt he'd rallied from difficulties with overall tyre grip. The Briton struggled throughout FP3 under braking, as the front tyres proved particularly lock-up prone and resulted in Hamilton enduring multiple excursions into the run-off. Hamilton landed in Q2 despite suffering floor damage in the opening stage of qualifying, but neither he nor Charles Leclerc were able to make their way into the top-10 shootout for pole. Hamilton appeared generally happy with his runs in Q2, which demonstrated few of the lock-ups characteristic of his lead-up to qualifying, but the Ferrari power unit's energy deployment seemed to hit its maximum sooner than the Mercedes and Red Bull-powered cars and inhibited straightline performance. Ferrari has been down on power versus those two manufacturers, and the long acceleration zone along the Strip exposed this deficit throughout the session. "We lost a piece of the floor on the first or second lap of Q1 and the car balance shifted, and we lost I think it was like three or four tenths of downforce we lost," Hamilton stated. "And then after that we were struggling more so with sliding, but it was basically from the get-go. Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari "And then my last lap was really good at the end, but I did the best I could with what I had. But then we lost something like six tenths just on deployment. So I think with that we would have been in Q3, but otherwise I was happy with my lap. "We knew long straights and stuff was going to be challenging. The gap seems to be a little bit more than I anticipated in a straight line. It's not insignificant. It's a big chunk on the straights. There had been a pervading sense that Ferrari would struggle in the low-temperature conditions in Las Vegas, as the team has struggled throughout 2026 to maintain tyre temperature through a qualifying lap. Hamilton agreed that the car was difficult to work with amid frequent sliding through the low-speed corners, especially after losing a chunk of floor, and only hopes that Ferrari can move forward in the Saturday night race as it aims to lock out second in the constructors' championship. "Just grip-wise, it just didn't feel like we had a ton of grip. We were struggling to get the tyres working and we were just kind of nowhere," he added. "These tyres have been very, very difficult this year to get working, even on hot surfaces. So it's definitely been difficult. I don't have any expectations [for the race]. Just trying to see if I can move forward." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Werder Bremen vs Hamburg preview: Derby Day in the North
item.description: Werder Bremen vs Hamburg preview: Derby Day in the North Werder Bremen Despite all the worry going into the campaign, this season has been a fantastic one so far for Werder Bremen. They were tipped as relegation candidates in the summer. It was a fair claim considering how badly the previous year went, and the amount of turnover that took place in the offseason. An injury to Jens Stage and an opening day blowout to Freiburg only further cemented those beliefs. However, things turned around very quickly for Bremen. They beat down RB Leipzig on matchday two, which began a seven-match unbeaten run. The team was scoring for fun, especially a returning Niclas Fullkrug who found the back of the net in every game during that spell. While there have been some slip-ups defensively, the back four and new number one Karl Hein are doing a solid enough job at that end of the pitch. Marco Friedl and Amos Pieper have formed a strong relationship. Both can be world class on their day, and if they are at their best then Werder are in pretty safe hands. This will be a big test for the club, though. While supporters are still thrilled with being far ahead of the bottom three, avoiding relegation is no longer the goal. Their sights are set much higher. The Green-Whites are in the thick of the European race, and the pressure is on to finally return to the international stage. Bremen are confident that their best would be more than enough to pick up a derby day win. However, they also know how often the team can fall flat, especially to start out games. If the hosts have a slow start, they’ll set themselves up for real disappointment. Then again, this is the exact contest the players and staff will be incredibly excited to start. Team news Werder are still without long-term absences like Felix Agu, Moussa N'Diaye, Jens Stage, Salim Musah, and Keke Topp. The real issue is with how many players are doubtful for the match, with Senne Lynen, Mitchell Weiser, and Marco Grull potentially missing out. item.title: Leclerc Says Ferrari Lost One Second on the Straight in Vegas—and Both Cars Missed Q3
item.description: Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton qualified 11th and 12th in Las Vegas on Friday, Ferrari’s first double Q2 exit since Imola in May 2025. Amid the chaos of tow and no-tow up and down the grid, Leclerc missed Q3 by 0.111 seconds and Hamilton by 0.167 seconds, while Kimi Antonelli took pole for Mercedes ahead of Saturday’s Las Vegas GP. Hamilton lacked grip throughout qualifying, while Leclerc was third-fastest in Q1 only to make a mistake in Q2. It is the first time this season that neither Ferrari has reached Q3. The last double Q2 exit was the 2025 Emilia Romagna GP, also in 11th and 12th, and before that the 2024 Canadian GP, with Leclerc and Carlos Sainz. Hamilton Lost Part of His Floor in Q1 Hamilton said floor damage early in Q1 cost him three or four tenths in downforce, and he told Sky Sports he lost more time to a lack of energy deployment at the end of his final lap. “Yeah, we lost a piece of the floor on the like first or second lap of Q1 and the car balance shifted,” he said after qualifying. “I think it’s like three or four tenths of the downforce we lost, and then after that we were struggling more so with sliding. But it was basically from the get-go, and then my last lap was really good at the end, but the best I could with what I had. “Then we lost something like six tenths or something around that time, so I think with that we would have been in Q3, but otherwise I was happy with my lap.” Asked about getting the tires warm on a cold Las Vegas night, he added: “These tires have been very, very difficult this year to get working, even on hot circuits, so it’s definitely been difficult.” Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas GP. Image Credit: Scuderia Ferrari Asked about both cars missing Q3, Hamilton said the gap on the straights was bigger than he had expected. “I don’t know, I mean, we knew long straights and stuff was going to be challenging,” he said. “The gap seems to be a little bit more than I anticipated in the straight line. “But yeah, I don’t know what it is; it’s not insignificant. It’s a big chunk on the straights, and then I don’t know; just grip-wise, it didn’t feel like we had a ton of grip, but we were struggling to get the tires working, and we were just kind of nowhere.” Leclerc Says Ferrari Lost One Second on the Straight Leclerc blamed his mistake in Q2 and a session spent managing traffic. “Yeah, I mean, I’m very disappointed as a whole,” he said. “Of course, there’s the mistake in Q2 that we paid the price for, but I think that is following a lot of frustration building up with a lot of mistakes with the way we managed everything, traffic and other things, and that doesn’t help, particularly on a track like this, where it’s all about tires. “You’ve got to put tires in the right window. I was looking more in my mirrors and trying to understand the traffic myself, which makes it very difficult to do anything. So, yeah, just very disappointed.” Charles Leclerc at the Las Vegas GP. item.title: Isack Hadjar: Red Bull "looked a bit stupid" in Vegas qualifying tow game
item.description: Motorsport photo Isack Hadjar has admitted that Red Bull "looked a bit stupid" in what became a tow battle at the end of Las Vegas Grand Prix qualifying. He says it "doesn't really matter" where he starts on Saturday night. Hadjar set the fifth-fastest time in Q3, 0.699s behind Kimi Antonelli, while team-mate Max Verstappen took pole after the Italian's five-place grid penalty. Hadjar moves up to fourth on the grid . The final runs in Q3 turned into a game of cat and mouse, as drivers attempted to position themselves in the tow of other drivers down the long straights of the Vegas circuit. While many achieved, Hadjar was left to rely on only his Ford power unit. "No, we had no tow. So yeah, we looked a bit stupid out there for the final run, but the other teams played it very smart, parking the car in Turn 1 while we were exiting the pit," Hadjar said. With nobody ahead of him, Hadjar said a good lap would have unraveled regardless with no tow on the straights, so he decided to abort. Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Asked whether Red Bull would play those games better next time, he admitted he'd rather just race and not rely on the gamble of such a scenario. "Yeah, I don't really like those games anyway. I like driving the car fast," he said. "There's just things you can't really control, and it's a bit like rolling the dice." "Yeah, so I don't really care. As long as I know I was quick around the corners, I'm happy about that. And in the end, we're starting fourth tomorrow, so we're in a good position for a podium." Hadjar was confident he had the pace to fight at the front, saying "I am definitely up there". "Job done on my side, and then I think it's a track where you can easily overtake with these massive straights and with the current regulations. So P4, P5, P2, it doesn't really matter in the end, so I'm happy," he said. Hadjar has three podiums in his first season with Red Bull, at Monaco, Azerbaijan and Sao Paulo, where he finished third behind Lando Norris and Verstappen. Another would be welcome for Red Bull, which is fighting for second in the constructors' championship and just 17 points ahead of McLaren , with just three races to go. Utah’s two-game winning streak came to an end with a 111-101 loss to the Phoenix Suns at the Delta Center, a game in which the Jazz struggled to find their shooting touch and spent much of the night trying to climb out of a double-digit hole. Utah made things interesting late, cutting Phoenix’s lead to four points at 105-101 with under a minute remaining, but the rally came too late and the Jazz couldn’t complete the comeback. Here are three takeaways from the loss. The Jazz dug themselves into another hole Utah had a chance to build on its back-to-back wins in Los Angeles, but the same issues that have haunted the team throughout the season showed up again at home. The Jazz turned the ball over 15 times, struggled to get stops in transition and left points at the free-throw line. Phoenix took advantage, building a lead as large as 16 points and forcing Utah to play catch-up for much of the night. The Jazz’s shooting certainly didn’t help. Utah finished a measly 10 of 39 from deep and left 13 points at the charity stripe. But head coach Will Hardy wasn’t interested in using the poor shooting as the only explanation for the loss. “Some nights when the shooting for us is this poor, it’s easy to point at that and say, ‘Oh, that’s why we lost,’” Hardy said. “We missed a bunch of free throws and open 3s.” Hardy noted the team has to understand the difference between what it can and can’t control. Players are trying to make shots, he said, but the Jazz still have to be better in areas that don’t depend on the ball going through the basket. “In particular tonight, I thought it was our transition defense and our rebounding,” Hardy said. The halfcourt offense still needs work The Jazz had opportunities to make a run, but too often the offense struggled to create anything easy. Utah finished with 35 made field goals on 84 attempts, shooting 42% from the field. Ace Bailey struggled mightily from downtown, finishing 0 for 7 from beyond the arc and 3 for 11 overall. The Jazz also struggled to generate enough movement and pressure around the basket to make Phoenix’s defense uncomfortable. The problem became more noticeable as the game went on. Utah spent long stretches working deep into the shot clock without finding a clean look, and the offense lacked the kind of quick, easy scoring that can help a team build momentum. Hardy said the Suns’ physicality bothered the Jazz more in the second half, which made it even harder for Utah to find a rhythm and turn its late push into a real comeback. item.title: George Russell: Las Vegas qualifying tow was "too difficult to orchestrate"
item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell claimed that getting the perfect tow in Las Vegas qualifying was "too difficult to orchestrate" after he missed out on pole position. Russell set the third-fastest time in Q3, 0.331 seconds behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli and 0.073s off Red Bull's Max Verstappen . He will start second, alongside Verstappen, after Antonelli's five-place grid penalty for power unit changes. A slipstream is worth a huge amount on the long straights of the Las Vegas Strip. Taking into account that Antonelli has been handed an engine penalty and won the drivers' championship in Mexico, Russell had been asking about getting a tow from his team-mate on his final run in qualifying. But as everyone piled out of the pits, the Italian driver ended up being the one to benefit from a tow rather than Russell. Asked by Sky Sports whether Mercedes' plans had worked, Russell said: "It was so difficult to orchestrate and getting the perfect tow is high risk. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes "Kimi, if he started his lap a second later, wouldn't have gone a lap in and in the end, he gained a second on the straight, maybe more and maybe lost six tenths in the corners. So it's unbelievable. "The impact overall, I'm still very pleased with the session because every lap today or this whole weekend, I've been pretty competitive." Addressing the chaotic start to the final flying laps, the Briton added: "I was very nervous when I left the pits on both occasions at the front of the pack. But it's too difficult to orchestrate when you've got some drivers doing a prep lap, other drivers going straight for it. Everyone's going for a tow. "There's a bit of a Mexican standoff. So in the end, it's high-risk, high-reward. And starting on the front row tomorrow, three races in a row we've been on the front row. So that's all right." With three rounds remaining in the 2026 season, Russell currently sits third in the drivers' championship, 17 points behind Verstappen in second and just one point ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in fourth. item.title: Oregon football handles business in drubbing of Michigan State
item.description: It wasn't always pretty, especially in the first half of a cold night in East Lansing, Michigan − a place the Oregon football team had never won in − but the No. 13 Ducks ultimately did what they had to do in a 45-7 demolition of Michigan State Nov. 20 at Spartan Stadium. All of the Ducks ' (8-3, 6-2 Big Ten) postseason aspirations are, somehow, still in front of them after another dominant win, though this time against a downtrodden Spartans (3-8, 1-7) squad. Previously dismissed as pretenders, UO is very much alive in the College Football Playoff race and put together another impressive result in Friday's expected drubbing. "We're starting to play our best football towards the end," quarterback Dylan Raiola said. "That's what coach Lanning wanted. He told us that before the season even started, and hopefully we get in this thing, because ... I think we'll take advantage of our opportunity." It didn't always look so dominant, especially in a first half littered with inconsistent play, and in particular in the offensive run game and in pass protection. Raiola was sacked three times in the first half and visibly frustrated with his offensive line, though eventually he settled in and completed 21 of 34 passes for 234 yards and a score. The Ducks lost yet another running back in Dierre Hill Jr. to an early injury but saw freshman Brandon Smith reignite the run game with 14 carries for 121 yards and two touchdowns. The defense, taking on a much-maligned MSU offense down to its third-string quarterback, was sometimes bend-but-don't-break but held the Spartans to just seven points and 200 yards of total offense. The Spartans averaged a measly 2.2 yards per rush attempt. Still, Oregon couldn't help but lament Michigan State's lone touchdown drive after allowing just one touchdown the week previous against Michigan. "Man, literally two plays away from two shutouts," senior defender A'Mauri Washington said. "It was just like, you want to get those plays back. It's the most simple things that we could have picked up and it could have led to a shutout. We just need to get over that hump." Brandon Smith a revelation for Oregon run game With yet another running back going down with an injury in Hill, and Jordon Davison out over the last three games, the freshman took advantage of his opportunity yet again in more of a starring role Friday night. "It's been great that Brandon's been getting more and more reps," Lanning said. In a season marred by inconsistent play along the offensive line throughout the first half of the season and with a pair of banged-up starters, Smith had the first 100-yard rushing game by a Duck this season in the win. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.title: How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊
item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
